title: Sorry Means Eighteen Different Things
style: gospel pop, 92 BPM, choir backing vocals, piano lead, building organ, hand claps, multi-accent narrators, comedic spoken interludes, EN/JP/FR/ES/DE/IT smatterings, big harmony chorus, theatrical comedy, hooky
lyrics:
[Intro — slow piano, polite throat-clearing]
Sorry. Sumimasen. Désolé. Lo siento.
Pardon. Perdón. Entschuldigung. Scusi.
And those are just the openers.

[Verse 1 — Canadian deadpan]
In Canada, "sorry" means "I exist near you"
Bumped into a wall — sorry to the wall, I do
Sorry I'm sorry, sorry I'm typing, sorry I breathe
The Canadian sorry is metabolic, it doesn't leave

[Pre-Chorus — building harmonies]
Sorry means I apologize
Sorry means excuse me, please
Sorry means I didn't hear
Sorry means come closer here

[Chorus — gospel-pop choir, big harmonies]
Sorry means eighteen different things!
Sorry's a verb, a noun, a way the language sings!
One word, eighteen meanings, depending on the tone
The English "sorry" never apologizes alone!

[Verse 2 — Japan masterclass]
"Sumimasen" in Tokyo does FOUR jobs at once
Sorry, excuse me, thank you, even hello, dunce
You bumped someone? Sumimasen
Someone helped you? Sumimasen
Calling a waiter? SUMIMASEN!
Saying it FOUR times in one minute is a Tuesday

[Verse 3 — British class system]
"Sorry" in London means "say that again, you're wrong"
"Sorry?" with the rising tone — that's where the daggers come along
"I'm SO sorry" means "you have offended my entire family line"
"Sorry sorry sorry" means we're British and it's fine

[Bridge — slow, cross-cultural]
Spanish has "lo siento" — I FEEL it, the loss
French "désolé" comes from desolate, deeply across
German "Entschuldigung" is six syllables of guilt
Italian "scusi" — light as the espresso they spilled

[Final Chorus]
Sorry means eighteen different things!
Sorry's a verb, a noun, a way the language sings!
One word, eighteen meanings, depending on the tone
The English "sorry" never apologizes alone!

[Outro — overlapping voices, fade]
Sorry. Sumimasen. Lo siento. Désolé. Scusi.
Sorry. Sorry. Sorry. Sorry.
[Canadian voice] Sorry about that.
